label: Köhler 1734: recover the literal colour-explanation argument
notes: The 1747 Bibliotheca Rinckiana synopsis reports Köhler regretting the loss of a German explanation of shield colours in the post-Siebmacher lineage, while the 1734 Weigel edition still lacked it. The literal Köhler wording has not yet been directly controlled.
reopen_rule: Inspect the 1734 Köhler preface and transcribe the colour passage with page locator. Search Farben-Erklärung, Farben, Tincturen, Buchstaben, Schraffierung, Siebmacher, Beschreibung, deutlich/klar, Mißverstand and related vocabulary.

label: Wappenkalender colour-key matrix/state history, 1728–1757
notes: Physical-copy controls repeatedly report a full-page engraved Erklärung der Farben; 1744 is directly inspected. Recurrent module identity is established, physical copper continuity is not.
reopen_rule: Compare high-resolution legend impressions from 1728, 1732, 1737, 1738, 1744, 1751, 1755 and 1757 for lettering, shield contours, spacing, dimensions, scratches, wear and retouching.

label: Does the central colour key consistently decode the annual armorial corpus?
notes: 1744 directly establishes legend plus immediately following hatching plus later prose blazon. Cross-year functional invariance has not yet been tested.
reopen_rule: Select recurring arms/fields representing Gold, Roth, Blau, Schwarz and Grün in at least three annuals and test actual hatch signs against each copy's central key and prose blazon.

label: Chronology of graphic key plus prose colour redundancy
notes: 1744 contains both centralized engraved decoder and alphabetical prose descriptions. It is unknown whether this redundant architecture is co-original to the late-1720s colour-key module or layered in later.
reopen_rule: Inspect contents/collation and prose blazon sections in 1728, 1732 and one later annual to date the coexistence of legend, hatching and verbal colour description.

label: 1772 publisher retrospective: colour-code failure and remedy
notes: The retrospective explicitly links letter-coded tinctures to Unordnung und Mißverstand within a broader diagnosis of compressed figures, inadequate description and historically changing arms. The colour-method question is what remedy the new publication architecture claims to provide.
reopen_rule: Produce page-level diplomatic transcription of the relevant Vorbericht passage and map each diagnosed failure to the replacement apparatus: hatching, colour key, prose descriptions, larger/changed format, cumulative/serial organisation.

label: Gatterer Synopsis: copy-level pigment census and information load
notes: Araújo establishes coloured, uncoloured and mixed surviving copies and argues that colour highlights boundaries/revolutions while line geometry remains load-bearing. The corpus needs explicit copy-level encoding of what pigment adds versus what survives without it.
reopen_rule: Create a copy census recording edition, library/shelfmark, table order, table-by-table colour presence, apparent colour categories, line information and whether historical interpretation changes when pigment is absent.

label: Gatterer Synopsis: exact semantics of assigned colours
notes: Secondary reconstructions assign specific colours to historical/political relations, but exact category semantics and copy invariance need primary table/legend control. Avoid repeating colour-to-status mappings from memory or secondary summaries without checking the relevant table and explanatory text.
reopen_rule: Inspect a coloured primary copy plus Gatterer's explanatory prose and encode each colour assignment with its literal historical relation and page/table locator.

label: Gatterer Heraldik: direct method statement on Tinkturen and Schraffierungen
notes: Searchable records and secondary quotations indicate Gatterer discusses tinctures, hatchings and additional signs associated with Rink, including historical evidence from old armorial sources. Direct primary-page control is required before using this as a method statement.
reopen_rule: Inspect the relevant pages in Abriß der Heraldik; transcribe Gatterer's evaluation of hatch systems, Naturfarbe/Eisenfarbe and any source-based rationale. Distinguish semantic category history from graphic notation choice.

label: Gatterer 1775: colour as a classificatory variable in Menschen- und Völkerkunde
notes: Modern scholarship reports that Gatterer's Menschen- und Völkerkunde begins with a geography of human bodies by shape and colour. This is a distinct colour regime from heraldic encoding and synchronistic-table syntax.
reopen_rule: Inspect Gatterer, Abriß der Geographie (1775), contents/method section and relevant chapter; transcribe the primary wording for Gestalt/Farbe and determine whether colour is observational, classificatory, causal, geographic or merely enumerative.

label: Did Gatterer transfer a colour method across heraldry, synchronistic history and Völkerkunde?
notes: The same author uses colour in at least three epistemically different settings, but no actor-level statement presently unifies them. Similarity of modern analytical vocabulary is not evidence of methodological transfer.
reopen_rule: Search Gatterer's methodological texts and cross-references for shared vocabulary of Farbe, Zeichen, Schraffierung, Unterschied, Vergleichung, Übersicht, Evidenz, Ordnung, Klasse, Kennzeichen and Darstellung. Promote only explicit conceptual or practical links.

label: Colour as a discriminator inside the Gatterer–Schlözer controversy
notes: The 1773 dispute demonstrably concerns priority, teaching and historical architecture. Colour may distinguish Gatterer's implementation of overview from Schlözer's, but the polemic has not yet been shown to debate colour directly.
reopen_rule: Search Schlözer Vorstellung/Species Facti and Gatterer Antwort plus programme texts for Farbe/color, Tafel, Gemälde, Karte, Zeichnung, illumin*, Übersicht, Plan and related media vocabulary. If no direct colour hit appears, retain colour as an analytical stress test rather than a polemical object.

label: Göttingen colour-order science and Gatterer's historical media: contact test
notes: Tobias Mayer, Erxleben and Lichtenberg place colour science and trichromatic/order problems inside the Göttingen milieu. Institutional coexistence alone does not establish transfer into Gatterer's historical practice.
reopen_rule: Look for citations, correspondence, common courses, Academy/Society interactions, shared publishers/instruments or explicit reference by Gatterer to Mayer/colour systems. Keep the background contextual unless a source establishes contact.

label: Historiographical gap test: monochrome chromatic decoders versus sample-based colour charts
notes: Simonini 2025 consolidates natural, pigmentary and trichromatic colour-chart histories, strongly centered on colour samples/reference systems. The Wappenkalender Erklärung der Farben instead translates colour categories into reproducible monochrome hatch signs and multilingual names.
reopen_rule: Search colour-chart/order historiography for heraldic hatching legends, tincture keys and other colourless colour-reference instruments. If absent, formulate the Wappenkalender object as a distinct chromatic decoder rather than forcing it into the sample-chart category.
